umf.visual.title: Curved captioned cross-region link
umf.visual.question: Which items are connected?
umf.visual.takeaway: A captioned data edge connects nodes in separate regions using named graphical endpoint anchors and a curved route.

source.view: The common witness supplies the node/edge identities, labels, caption, data kind, region membership and region labels. The synthetic native witness supplies rectangle symbols, the curved route, and exact endpoint attachment strings. This review retains east-port and west-port as node-local graphical anchor IDs and authors east/west side hints from their names; the witness has no native port objects or side declarations. Exact connector control points and item coordinates remain native-only.

omissions: The common and native inputs are synthetic witnesses. They do not establish deployed system semantics or describe a private original Miro board.

The synthetic native witness explicitly records a curved route and attachment strings east-port and west-port. This review retains those strings as local graphical anchor IDs; its side values are review-authored hints guided by the names, not native side fields, native port objects, exact physical sides, or business/service interfaces. Exact native control points and geometry remain in the companion witness.
The common source explicitly supplies the two region groups and each node membership. Exact group bounds and item coordinates are not represented in the shared model.

Historical Miro and Google Slides restored-original previews and the PowerPoint/LibreOffice preview use Visual 1.0.0. They are provenance for the older shared source, not qualification evidence for Visual 1.4 curved routing or endpoint ports. The PowerPoint preview is a LibreOffice conversion, not a PowerPoint screenshot.
